name: MINSIS
summary: MINSIS was a proposed short-baseline tau-neutrino appearance experiment near the Fermilab NuMI source. The 2009 workshop and 2010 report studied how tau detection could probe non-standard flavour transitions.
detection_principle: An emulsion cloud chamber or related high-resolution silicon/emulsion detector would resolve short tau decays in neutrino interactions near the source. A prompt tau-flavour component over such a short distance could test interactions or mixing beyond the standard long-baseline oscillation expectation.

status.label: Proposed
status.evidence: The primary report describes a proposal under discussion, and the INFN catalogue lists the programme among expired projects. No operating MINSIS detector is established.

timeline.event: Madrid workshop examined physics reach and detector requirements.

collaboration.name: MINSIS Collaboration

key_parameters.name: Studied baseline scale
key_parameters.value: Approximately 1 km in representative near-detector calculations

key_parameters.name: Detector options
key_parameters.value: Emulsion cloud chamber, silicon, or hybrid silicon-emulsion designs

results.summary: Compared possible detectors, non-standard-interaction models and projected sensitivities. The figures are phenomenological forecasts rather than measured appearance signals.

science_scope: This dossier preserves a named historical proposal. Design parameters and sensitivity estimates are not measured neutrino results; later programmes using the same laboratory or technology are distinct.

media.caption: Illustrative non-standard-interaction appearance probabilities in the MINSIS workshop report; theoretical curves, not measured data.
